coordinateBasis: Rounded J2000/ICRS catalogue centres for a small orientation finder; not telescope pointing or photometric predictions.

targets.name: M31 · Andromeda Galaxy
targets.hint: Start in Andromeda; diffuse extended light, with a brighter core. Dark skies and a wide field help.

targets.name: M42 · Orion Nebula
targets.hint: Below Orion’s belt, in the sword. Optical detail depends on conditions and equipment.

targets.name: M45 · Pleiades
targets.hint: A broad cluster in Taurus. Binoculars offer a wider overview than high magnification.

targets.name: M13 · Hercules Cluster
targets.hint: In Hercules. Binoculars may show a patch; resolving individual stars needs suitable optics.

targets.name: M57 · Ring Nebula
targets.hint: Between the southern stars of Lyra. Small target; a telescope and finder practice are useful.

targets.name: M1 · Crab Nebula
targets.hint: Start near Zeta Tauri, the tip of the Bull’s southern horn. A small telescope and dark sky help with the faint patch.

targets.name: M3 · Globular Cluster
targets.hint: Sweep roughly halfway from Arcturus toward Cor Caroli. Try binoculars for the glow and a small telescope for a closer look.

targets.name: M4 · Globular Cluster
targets.hint: Look just west of Antares. Try binoculars under dark skies when this part of Scorpius is highest.

targets.name: M5 · Globular Cluster
targets.hint: Use 5 Serpentis as a nearby guide star. Binoculars can show a fuzzy spot under dark skies.

targets.name: M8 · Lagoon Nebula
targets.hint: Sweep above the Sagittarius Teapot’s spout. Start with binoculars or a wide, low-power telescope view under dark skies.

targets.name: M11 · Wild Duck Cluster
targets.hint: Follow the Milky Way down from the tail of Aquila into Scutum. Look for a compact patch in binoculars.

targets.name: M15 · Pegasus Globular Cluster
targets.hint: Trace the horse’s head out from the Great Square and sweep beyond Enif. Try binoculars for a small fuzzy spot.

targets.name: M22 · Globular Cluster
targets.hint: Start just northeast of Kaus Borealis, the star at the top of the Teapot. Try binoculars near the cluster’s highest point.

targets.name: M27 · Dumbbell Nebula
targets.hint: Start at the tip of Sagitta’s arrow and move north. A small telescope and dark skies help show the nebula’s shape.

targets.name: M33 · Triangulum Galaxy
targets.hint: Sweep northwest from Alpha Trianguli with wide binoculars on a dark, moonless night. Its diffuse glow fades easily under light pollution.

targets.name: M34 · Open Cluster
targets.hint: Sweep between Algol and Almach. Use binoculars to look for a loose group of stars.

targets.name: M35 · Shoe Buckle Cluster
targets.hint: Start near the Twins’ feet, close to Eta Geminorum. Binoculars suit the broad cluster.

targets.name: M36 · Pinwheel Cluster
targets.hint: Sweep inside Auriga’s pentagon for the middle of the M36–M38 trio. Try binoculars or a low-power eyepiece.

targets.name: M37 · Open Cluster
targets.hint: Look just outside the pentagon on the side facing Gemini. Try binoculars first, then low power for the dense star field.

targets.name: M38 · Starfish Cluster
targets.hint: From M36, sweep northwest inside Auriga. Wide binoculars help compare both clusters.

targets.name: M41 · Little Beehive Cluster
targets.hint: Sweep about four degrees south of Sirius. Try binoculars when Canis Major is high and clear of your horizon.

targets.name: M44 · Beehive Cluster
targets.hint: Sweep the middle of Cancer between Gemini and Leo. Binoculars frame the broad cluster well.

targets.name: M51 · Whirlpool Galaxy
targets.hint: Start near Alkaid at the end of the Big Dipper’s handle. Try a small telescope at a dark site for the cores.

targets.name: M81 · Bode’s Galaxy
targets.hint: Extend the line from Phecda through Dubhe. Look for M81 and M82 as a pair in a wide, low-power telescope view.

targets.name: M82 · Cigar Galaxy
targets.hint: Find M81 first and look about half a degree north for the thin streak. Start with low power at a dark site.

landmarks.name: Orion · Alnilam, belt centre
landmarks.hint: Middle star of Orion’s three-star belt. The nebula lies in the sword below the belt.

landmarks.name: Lyra · Vega
landmarks.hint: Bright anchor for Lyra; use the small parallelogram to work towards M57.

landmarks.name: Ursa Minor · Polaris
landmarks.hint: Northern-sky anchor near the celestial pole. Not visible from most southern latitudes.

landmarks.name: Ursa Major · Dubhe
landmarks.hint: One of the Big Dipper’s bowl stars; the Dipper is an asterism within Ursa Major.

landmarks.name: Carina · Canopus
landmarks.hint: Bright southern-sky anchor in Carina; unavailable from far northern latitudes.
